News.title: Scientists say rat virus is mutating - but no critical changes yet
News.content:
“We see two particular small mutations in two patients… [but] there’s no changes in the behavior of the virus,” Dr Oude Munnink told the Telegraph. “It’s typical of viruses, because they of course evolve and they make mistakes during their replication.”

Once inside a human or animal cell, viruses replicate at speed. During this process, small errors in the genetic code can emerge – over time, they can build up to change how the pathogen behaves. This occurred during the coronavirus pandemic, when new variants like delta and omicron emerged as Sars-Cov-2 tore through millions of people.

But the Andes hantavirus is not Covid-19, Dr Oude Munnink said. Not only is a dramatic genetic leap less likely when tens rather than millions of people are infected, but the virus itself is thought to be more stable.

The latest samples are “reassuringly” similar to sequences from an outbreak in Argentina in 2018-2019, when 34 people were infected and 11 died in a “super-spreading” event, said Dr Damien Tully, an associate professor in bioinformatics at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.

“Preliminary analyses indicate only a relatively small degree of change,” he said. “At present, there is no clear evidence… of major genetic shifts, unusual evolution, or reassortment.”

Tracking hantavirus in rats

Still, scientists are concerned about the potential genetic progression of the Andes virus in its primary host: the long-tailed pygmy rice rat.

The small rodent is found in parts of Argentina and Chile, mainly in the temperate forests and humid grasslands of the Patagonian-Andean region.

“The main virus evolution is occurring now in a wildlife reservoir,” said Dr Oude Munnink. “It’s important to do studies in this wildlife reservoir to see the distribution and the viral evolution of this virus in [rats]... I think that’s information we are lacking at the moment.”

Hantavirus cases in Argentina have recently surged, and researchers are now investigating whether this is a statistical blip, a reflection of improved diagnostics, or something more ominous.

Earlier this month, the Ministry of Health said there have been 101 cases since June 2025, around twice as many cases as the year before. The virus, which causes a severe lung disease called hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, killed roughly a third of patients.

Some scientists say changes in land use, including deforestation, may have driven rats into closer contact with people and into new regions. The country has also seen a rise in extreme weather – including a major drought and bouts of intense rainfall – that may have pushed the long-tailed pygmy rice rats out of their usual habitats as they search for food.

But genetic changes cannot yet be ruled out, said Dr Oude Munnink. He compared controlling the Andes virus to the Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (Mers), which is endemic in camels across the Gulf. The fatality rate in humans is roughly 35 per cent.

“I think [the hantavirus] is more or less similar to Mers… that’s circulating in the dromedary reservoir. And of course, the more virus is circulating, the higher chances that there will be mutations,” Dr Oude Munnink said.

“There is a concern, always, that there might be sporadic spillovers. But I think that if we have our diagnostics up and running and we detect the virus if it affects humans… at an early time point, that we still might be able to control the further spread.

“But it does highlight that it might be important to really get your diagnostics assays also Argentina up and running,” he said.

That begins with understanding where the virus is circulating in Argentina, how it is behaving and whether it has changed.

As a starting point, researchers are trying to pinpoint the origins of the latest outbreak. At first, a leading hypothesis suggested the Dutch couple who died from Andes virus contracted it while bird watching near a landfill site on the outskirts of Ushuaia – a port where MV Hondius docked, on the southern tip of Argentina.

Yet the long-tailed pygmy rice rat traditionally lives at least 1,000 miles away in Patagonian Andes, as well as north-western Argentina.

News.title: The race to understand how rat-virus spreads
News.content:
The right landing place

Even a large dose of the hantavirus delivered via some good-sized droplets may not be enough if the virus lands in the wrong place.

Viruses must lock onto human cells and start to replicate for a person to become infected.

SARS-CoV-2 was very good at locking on to cells in the upper respiratory tract around the nose and throat.

The Andes virus locks onto endothelial cells - the thin, flat cells that line the inside of our blood vessels.

These are harder for a virus to access than respiratory cells, as they are usually cased in a protective layer and to reach them, a pathogen first has to successfully infect and destroy the surrounding cells before they can cause real damage.

A related variable here is the individual’s own immune system. It is likely, as with most diseases, that some people are more vulnerable than others.

People with diabetes, obesity, and hypertension are more likely to have endothelial dysfunction, for example, making the cells which hantavirus typically locks onto more vulnerable to invasion.

Age, fitness and previous exposure to different viruses can all also play a part, but so can simple genetics.

During the Covid-19 pandemic, for instance, there was evidence that people of South Asian origin were more vulnerable to developing severe disease because of a specific, inherited genetic trait.

The LZTFL1 gene was found to impair the lung lining’s response to the virus, and is thought to be carried by roughly 60 per cent of people of South Asian descent.

The carrier

Another vital variable is the carrier, when exactly they become infectious and how they behave.

In the Argentinian outbreak of 2018 studied by scientists, the researchers concluded that the people who spread the virus to others were all “symptomatic” at the point at which they infected others.

But defining if someone is symptomatic is not as easy, as it’s on a spectrum.

A person with a tickle at the back of their throat may have the symptoms of a cold, but so does someone with a temperature who is coughing and sneezing frequently.

“Patient 2 was the most likely source for six infections in other persons during the early prodromal phase because of his active social life,” noted the researchers who unpicked the 2018 outbreak in Argentina.

The medical term “prodromal” refers to the period between the first recognition of a disease’s symptom and its more severe form.

Scientists will be poring over this and other evidence to try and understand if something resembling asymptomatic spread is possible.

Given the virus’s lengthy incubation period – which can last up to 8 weeks – it will be extremely important for investigators to know when exactly people with the virus become infectious.

Currently, most experts think there is little to no risk of hantavirus spreading asymptomatically, but they said the same of Sar-COv-2 initially, and it can not yet be ruled out.

Professor Devi Sridhar, chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh, told The Telegraph: “I’m always erring on the side of caution: I think we can say that we hope that there’s no asymptomatic or presymptomatic transmission. But I don’t think we should assume anything like that.”

Referencing the 20 British patients now isolating back in the UK after being repatriated by the Foreign Office, Dr Cariad Evans, an NHS Consultant in virology at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals, said: “As the UK contacts are currently asymptomatic, they should not pose a risk of onward transmission to others, and therefore the risk to the UK public is very low.”

News.title: Southampton reach play-off final – but may be thrown out
News.content:
A place in the Championship play-off final is at stake on the south coast as Southampton host Middlesbrough at St Mary’s, with off-field matters being talked about as much as matters on the pitch. The first leg up in the north East on Saturday ended in a 0-0 draw but the build-up to the first leg was dominated by ‘spygate’. Middlesbrough claimed that a member of the Southampton coaching staff was found watching and recording a training session at the Middlesbrough training ground a few days before the first leg.

Southampton reached the play-off final two years ago, beating West Brom in the semi-final before overcoming Leeds in the final at Wembley. Tonda Eckert’s side are currently on a 20-game unbeaten run in the league, with their last defeat at St Mary’s coming back in January.

“We are at half-time now and I think you can interpret this in many different ways,” Southampton boss Tonda Eckert told BBC Radio Solent. “In the end it is important that we bring it to our side on Tuesday [tonight] and I think that the crowd and the supporters are going to give us a very big lift. The boys were outstanding over 90 minutes [on Saturday] and we take lots of the positives into the game on Tuesday [tonight].”

Since the early part of January, Middlesbrough’s only defeat away from home was at Championship winners Coventry. Middlesbrough did finish level on points with Southampton during the regular season.

“We are strong away from home, we have lost one of our 10 games,” Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg told BBC Radio Tees. “We have scored against every team since then, we know we are a very good football team. There was a lot of confidence from the performance [in the first leg] and we’ll use that going into this game and we know we can beat every team in this league. A lot of people like the way we play football. It is a very brave way of doing it. That first half of the play-off game was unbelievable. There are many that like the way we play, like the way we handle ourselves. We are honest in our approach in trying to play offensive football and there are a lot of people that like that.”

Hellberg has confirmed that midfielder Hayden Hackney, who has been linked with a move to Crystal Palace this summer, is still out with a calf injury.

The winner tonight will face Hull in the play-off final after they beat Millwall 2-0 on aggregate. Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: World Cup 2026: Everything you need to know
News.content:
How can I watch the World Cup on television?

BBC Sport and ITV have once again split the matches between them, with two of England’s group matches on ITV (the first against Croatia and third against Panama) and one on BBC (the second match against Ghana). The final will be shown on both channels simultaneously.

Since the 1998 World Cup, England’s win percentage at major tournaments is considerably better on BBC, leading to fears of an “ITV curse”.

Scotland’s group games follow the reverse pattern, with their group-stage opener against Haiti and third match against Brazil on BBC and the middle game against Morocco on ITV.

For the first time, parts of the World Cup will be free to watch on YouTube after Fifa struck an agreement with the streaming platform. The first 10 minutes of every game will be streamed live on YouTube, with broadcasters sharing a select number of full matches on the website. “Content creators” will be part of the coverage as Fifa seeks to attract a new generation of fans.

Fan groups demanded an immediate halt to World Cup ticket sales last December, accusing Fifa of charging “extortionate” prices to the most dedicated supporters.

Football Supporters Europe (FSE), which represents groups across the continent, called for sales via the likes of the Football Association to be suspended when it emerged that watching England at next summer’s tournament could end up costing at least £5,000.

According to FSE, the minimum $6,900 (£5,143) fans would have to pay to follow their country from their first match until the final was nearly five times as much as during the last World Cup.

In response to growing public pressure, Fifa announced a cheaper band of £45 tickets would be made available, but only for a small percentage of seats.

In the latter stages of the tournament, the majority of the cheapest tickets are £686 for the semi-final and £3,119 for the final, pricing condemned by the Football Supporters Association’s Fan Embassy.

“Surprise surprise Fifa are finding out that supporters will turn their backs on ludicrous prices, however prestigious the game. Thousands of pounds for any football match is beyond greedy,” a statement said.

“The most loyal fans, be they English supporters or those of any other nationality, are being priced out.

The final phase of ticket sales will be last-minute general sales, where any remaining tickets are offered on a first-come, first-served basis. This phase will begin in April, and you can access the ticket portal on Fifa’s website here.

There are fears that this World Cup could prove the most expensive ever for supporters, with Fifa operating “dynamic pricing” and taking a 15 per cent fee on resale tickets from both buyer and seller.

Sports.title: World Cup boss slams national team stars as he brands Arsenal hero ‘self-absorbed’ and ex-Chelsea ace ‘complete idiot’
Sports.content:
EX-FRANCE boss Raymond Domenech sensationally let rip at Thierry Henry, Nicolas Anelka and others in his secret World Cup diary.

Domenech, 74, was at the helm when Les Bleus finished bottom of their group at the South Africa tournament in 2010 and flew home in disgrace.





France were among the favourites to win it after losing to Italy in the final four years prior.

Their squad boasted superstars like Franck Ribery and Karim Benzema, as well as Premier League legends Henry, Anelka, Patrice Evra and Samir Nasri.

But any hint of dressing room harmony was ripped apart when players refused to train after Anelka was sent home.

The ex-Chelsea striker was banished after allegedly telling Domenech during a half-time spat: “Go f*** yourself, you dirty son of a w****.”



Domenech and Evra both denied hearing Anelka say those words but the publication that reported it, L’Equipe, was acquitted in court after a legal challenge for running the story.

Now, a Netflix documentary titled ‘The Bus: The Blues on Strike’ has delved deeper into the turmoil.

And Domenech handed over the private diary he kept up during the course of the tournament to producers.

In it, he called Arsenal legend Henry a “banal, self-absorbed Leo.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Anelka was branded a “complete idiot” for walking past Domenech without looking at him.

The manager wrote that the best thing for ex-Manchester United star Evra would have been “to keep quiet”.



Former Lyon midfielder Yoann Gourcuff was labelled a “complete moron”.

And on the entire squad, Domenech admitted: “I sometimes have bursts of hatred towards these idiots.”

The veteran manager even sarcastically praised the players for finally coming together to take strike action.

He wrote: “This is your best collective effort of the entire World Cup. Suicide has been committed! Hallelujah!”

Domenech was dismissed without compensation for gross misconduct after the tournament, with French football authorities citing his handling of Anelka’s dismissal and the team strike as reasons for their decision.



But Domenech did eventually reach a compensation agreement after mounting a legal challenge against the French Football Federation.

Sports.title: Casemiro reveals moment Michael Carrick ‘killed’ Man Utd stars ‘with class’ after agonising defeat
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO opened up on Michael Carrick’s dressing room methods and how he rallies his Man Utd stars after a shock loss.

Speaking on Rio Ferdinand Presents, the former footballer asked Casemiro if Carrick ever goes crazy at the players.





But the Man Utd midfielder was quick to explain: “Oh, no, no, no, no, he stays calm every time.

“He has class. I like it. I remember in the game at Newcastle, we lost this game.

“He killed everyone, but with class, with class. He killed us, but with class. So for me, he’s a very good manager.”

The Red Devils suffered a surprise loss to Newcastle in March after Anthony Gordon converted his spot-kick at the very end of the first half and William Osula scored in the last minute of normal time.

While Old Trafford‘s Brazilian talisman recovered one, it was not enough to seal a point on the road.

Casemiro has scored nine times in United’s 40-game season with two assists.

The former Real Madrid ace has helped his side secure Champions League football for the 2026/27 campaign but he will still leave this summer.

It has been a turbulent few years for United but unless Liverpool catch them on the final day, they will finish third in the same spot as the 2022/23 season.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The North-West outfit only need ONE point from their final two games to be certain of third place.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada are expected to recommend front-runner Carrick for the permanent role to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

The club have not held any formal discussions with external coaches, having appointed the interim boss for the rest of the season on January 13.

But United insist no deal has been agreed with any coach to take charge next season.



Old Trafford’s hierarchy will still hold a meeting at the end of the season.

Key United players Amad and Matheus Cunha have thrown their support behind Carrick, with Cunha claiming Carrick gives off “a Sir Alex Ferguson vibe”.

Sports.title: Man Utd academy aces reveal the first-team stars set to inspire them to FA Youth Cup glory against Man City
Sports.content:
BEYOND the star power of JJ Gabriel and Chido Obi, sit plenty of hidden gems vying for Youth Cup glory.

Rafe McCormack and Yuel Helafu are two players who are flying under the radar for Darren Fletcher‘s Under-18s at Manchester United.





The next stage of their development brought a new experience: their first Carrington interview, previewing the first all-Manchester Youth Cup final since 1986.

Speaking in the refurbished room Sir Alex Ferguson used for interviews, Helfau said: “It’s every team’s cup final when they play against us.

“We’ve got to use that to our advantage and hopefully play with freedom and win the game.”

Having seamlessly jumped between age groups this season, the duo could also be drafted into the Under-21 Premier League 2 final a mere 48 hours after their Youth Cup showdown.

Helafu in particular, a right back who follows the Reece James trend of a full-back inverting into midfield, has stoodout and recently joined the first team’s training camp in Ireland.

Just five days after defeating Crystal Palace in the Youth Cup semi-finals, Fletcher’s side lost the Under-18 League Cup final on penalties at Selhurst Park.

Helafu said: “We are trying to use that pain that we felt to make sure that we don’t lose in the next final. Training has been good and we feel confident.”

While McCormack added: “It was disappointing to lose on penalties but it’s made us stronger, we’ve taken the learnings from that into this final.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The academy prospects have benefited from a welcoming senior set-up, receiving direct mentorship from the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Diogo Dalot and Mason Mount.

The 17-year-old duo have both made Under 21 debuts this season and are excited to wear the classic club suits as they head across to City’s Joie Stadium on Thursday night.

And the pros are dedicated to supporting it. Senne Lammens went to watch the quarter-final at Old Trafford, while United sources revealed Bruno Fernandes often streams the games in the team hotel.

Helafu said: “Players like Tom Heaton and obviously Michael Carrick watch all the games, so we’ve got their support and we just want to impress them.”



Helafu was one of three academy stars called up to Carrick’s training camp in County Kildare in April, while McCormack expressed his “nerves” before his debut session.

Helafu said: “Zirkzee is very good with me, always very welcoming, and very funny. Martinez as well.

“As a defender Martinez gives me tips because I’m not the biggest, but he gives me different advice to use when I’m marking someone bigger. But everyone is top, everyone is welcoming.”

Meanwhile, traditional No6 McCormack was in awe to train with Casemiro, pointing to his “five Champion League titles”.

He said: “Every time I go to the first team, I try to learn from Kobbie Mainoo and Casemiro. I remember speaking to Mason about passing through lines and he’s very helpful.”



Helafu pointed to United’s second-longest serving player Dalot as an unrated player who he learning off.

He said: “‘I think he’s genuinely so good and he’s a great leader as well.



“I remember there was one training session and I was in front of him and he was just talking me through the whole session, just making sure I’m pressing in the right way getting up to the ball, keeping the ball, everything.”

Helafu and McCormack were both among the 67,000 at Old Trafford when Mainoo and Alejandro Garnacho lifted the club’s eleventh Youth Cup in 2022.

McCormack said: “We saw how big it was and how much it much it meant for the players. For us to be in the final now just means, it means a lot.”

Both players have been struck by the sheer size of the Old Trafford pitch across their four appearances there since December.

Helafu said: “It’s massive. I got cramp after 65 minutes and the ball was moving slow, so you have to punch the pass in.”



McCormack has been on United’s books since he was eight years old having gone between Manchester City and Everton, while Helafu was scouted at Under-10s.

The teenagers were unfazed about City switching the final venue away from the Etihad to the club’s 7,000 academy stadium inside the training complex.

Helafu said: “We aren’t too bothered as long as our family can come down and watch and we’ve got a pitch to play on, we will be fine.”

McCormack added: “It would have been a bonus to play in the first team stadium, but to us it doesn’t matter. We’re just focusing on winning the trophy most importantly. We’re just excited to play.”

Despite the final being held in front of a smaller crowd, the BBC have agreed a deal with TNT to stream the match for free.



Fittingly for unsung heroes, the duo were quick to share the spotlight by singling out some of their lesser-known team-mates.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Helafu said: “You’ve got Junior [Brown] off the wing. He’s top and I normally play with him, so he’s very good. Albert [Mills] as well, a rock at the back.”

Brown scored the winner in United’s 3-2 win over Sunderland in the Youth Cup quarters at Old Trafford. Obi has four Youth Cup goals, while JGabriel has three.

And in the spirit of the pinnacle of American sport, the Super Bowl, the fixture will feature a half-time show promising some of the biggest names in music.

Coldplay were announced to be headlining the show last year, but were said to be incorporating a number of other artists into their performance.

And now the list has been revealed thanks to a video featuring Coldplay frontman Chris Martin and Sesame Street character Elmo, published to the children’s show’s official X account.

The bizarre pairing teamed up to announce that not only would Elmo and the Cookie Monster be joining Martin and Co on stage, but a host of music stars.



First among them is World Cup music icon Shakira, whose song Waka Waka was the official song for the 2010 South Africa World Cup.

The Colombian is also releasing an anthem for this year’s tournament, titled Dai Dai.

Sports.title: Florentino Perez claims he’s FOUND Real Madrid dressing room mole who leaked bust-up between Valverde and Tchouameni
Sports.content:
FLORENTINO PEREZ reckons he has found the mole leaking secrets from the Real Madrid dressing room.

News of a physical training ground bust-up between Aurelien Tchouameni and Fede Valverde that left the latter in hospital spread like wildfire last week.





Valverde later claimed that he had “accidentally hit a table” and had not been punched by his team-mate despite suffering from head trauma.

But the Uruguayan also said: “Clearly, someone is spreading rumours.”

Bernabeu president Perez has been tasked with steadying the ship after a turbulent couple of weeks in the Spanish capital.

And he insists progress has been made in rooting out the mole.



Perez told TV channel La Sexta: “Several players have fought every year – when it’s public, it’s because someone wanted [people] to know.

“We have an idea [of who it is]. After this, everything is chaos, it’s ruin.”

Tchouameni and Valverde were each fined an eye-watering £440,000 for their scrap, which was thought to be sparked by a strong tackle in training.

Their unsavoury incident is just one part of the mess and uncertainty that surrounds Real.

Sports.title: Motherwell vs Celtic penalty flashpoint dubbed ‘the WORST VAR decision ever seen’ as pundits react to controversial call
Sports.content:
THE FOOTBALL world has been reacting to the hugely controversial call that saw Celtic awarded a penalty in stoppage time at Fir Park.

Pundits here in Scotland and from further afield have had their say, as have the two managers involved in the title race.





Motherwell‘s Sam Nicholson was adjudged to have handled the ball in the 96th minute of the match against Celtic.

Kelechi Iheanacho stepped up from the subs’ bench to tuck the spot kick beyond Calum Ward, sparking a mini pitch invasion from the travelling Hoops fans who celebrated an improbable 3-2 victory.

Debate has since raged about whether the ball did in fact come off Nicholson’s hand or if it only hit his head.

John Beaton didn’t point to the spot on the field but after being recommended to review the incident on the monitor by VAR, he wasted little time in changing his mind.

Derek McInnes described it as DISGUSTING.

Martin O’Neill insisted it was a clear penalty.

Jens Berthel Askou said: “I can’t see in any world where it could ever be a penalty. It’s one of the worst decisions I have seen in my career in football.”

Speaking on Twitter, footie icon Gary Lineker called it perhaps the WORST decision he’s ever seen VAR make.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

He posted: “This might be the worst VAR decision I’ve seen (and there’s a lot of competition). Extraordinary given the significance.”

Soccer Saturday TV legend Jeff Stelling replied: “He heads it.”

Before adding: “Seriously that is never a handball at Fir Park. The boy headed it 20 yards. The ref takes one look after VAR calls him over. Embarrassing for Scottish football.”

And the Scottish Sun’s resident tipster Jim Delahunt said: “Got to agree with Gary on this one. Not anti Celtic. Not pro Hearts. Just sad for the game.”

Ex-Hearts, Sunderland and Wolverhampton star Stephen Elliott alleged that the dubious penalty award amounted to cheating.



He said: “That is cheating pure and simple. That cannot be a penalty. For the love of God. Game is gone!”

Meanwhile in the Sky Sports studio, the punditry trio of John Robertson, Paul Hartley and Kris Boyd were unanimous in their verdict.

All three felt the penalty SHOULDN’T have been given.

Robertson, Hearts‘ all-time top scorer, began: “I don’t know if it has actually hit his hand.

“Look at the power he’s got on it. That looks like a header.



“I’m not looking at it through maroon-tinted spectacles, his hand is up and if it’s hit his hand then of course it’s a penalty.

“But look at the power he gets on that. That’s a head!

“I didn’t see too many Celtic players claiming for it.

“I don’t think this is a handball. It heads his head!”

He added: “He’s not given it on the pitch and it has to be a clear and obvious error.



“That is not a clear and obvious.

“I don’t see what Andrew Dallas has seen to call him over.”

Thanks to Iheanacho’s goal, Celtic know that victory at home against Hearts would see them retain their crown and deny Hearts a fairy tale story.



McInnes’ men won 3-0 at home to Falkirk with strikes from Stuart Findlay, Cammy Devlin and Blair Spittal.

The Jambos are bidding to end 66 years without a league title win and put a stop to 41 years of Old Firm dominance.

Success for the Tynecastle side would be akin to the upset Leicester City caused by winning the Premier League in 2016.

Robertson continued: “That’s why, from a Hearts perspective, you’re raging tonight.

“Knowing Celtic needed a 3-0 win is totally different to what will transpire on Saturday now.”



Robertson cautioned that he didn’t want viewers to think he was viewing the incident through maroon-tinted spectacles.

But ex-Rangers and Kilmarnock star Boyd rushed to reassure him that wasn’t the case.

He also pointed to the failure to award Hearts a penalty on Saturday night when Tawanda Maswanhise appeared to trip Alexandros Kyziridis – a decision that Willie Collum sympathised with McInnes on – and Celtic’s Alistair Johnston escaping a red card for his tackle on Mikey Moore in Sunday’s Old Firm derby.

Boyd said: “You’re not seeing it through maroon-tinted spectacles. For that to fly off his head at that pace – if your hand hits a ball, it’s just going to drop right in front of you, it’s not going to fly off you like that.

“And I tell you, that’s three massive calls in the last few games.



“The penalty kick at Motherwell on Saturday night, the red card against Alistair Johnston and that there tonight. It’s incredible.

“There will be serious questions asked about it. Rightfully so.

“We all can’t be wrong. There’s no way John Beaton can look at that and be certain.”

He added: “It’s impossible to get that amount of distance on that with your hand.”

Hartley, who played for Hibs, Hearts and Celtic during his playing career, expanded on the theory that for Nicholson to have generated such purchase on the ball, he couldn’t have handled it.



He said: “The power on it, it’s clearly came off his head.

“The view we’ve got there is quite difficult, if it was from behind we would have a better view.

“You can’t generate that power with your hand to put it back out for a throw in.

“Celtic have got a wee bit lucky there.

“I don’t know what John Beaton has seen.



“You look at the timing of the error. It’s a massive call.”

Meanwhile over on BBC Sportsound, another former Hearts man was unhappy.

Ryan Stevenson said the decision was “garbage” and that it was a “disgrace” that John Beaton didn’t spend more time at the monitor.

He compared it to the amount of time it took for a final decision to be reached during West Ham vs Arsenal last weekend.

Ex-Celtic defender Darren O’Dea says by the letter if the law it should be a penalty, but questioned if the video evidence was conclusive.



On talkSPORT however, Jamie O’Hara said it WAS a penalty while co-host of the Sports Bar Jason Cundy disagreed.

Cundy said: “I’ve just watched it again, that’s not a pen.

“Where’s the pen?

“That’s an absolute disgrace.

“Shocking. There’s foul. There’s no handball.”



While O’Hara said: “It looks like his hand is on his head and he’s headed his hand.”

Cundy retorted: “He heads the ball. His hand is in front of his face.

“There’s nothing going on there to give a penalty.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“They’ve made that up. I think that’s AI!”

Sports.title: Hearts boss Derek McInnes blasts ‘DISGUSTING’ Celtic penalty award as Motherwell’s Askou asks ‘what are we doing here?’
Sports.content:
HEARTS boss Derek McInnes has blasted the last gasp decision to award Celtic a penalty at Motherwell as DISGUSTING.

The Jambos looked set to extend their lead over the Hoops in the title battle until late, late chaos in North Lanarkshire.





Hearts had already beaten Falkirk 3-0 when play was raging on at Motherwell.

Jambos players and fans were all keeping an eye out for the final score at Fir Park where it was level at 2-2.

Then, drama.

With Hearts hoping for a Motherwell goal that would’ve clinched them the title, instead it was Celtic who won it.

And in hugely controversial circumstances.

VAR told referee John Beaton to delay proceedings as they surveyed an incident in the box.

Celtic’s Auston Trusty was down but it soon transpired VAR official Andrew Dallas was looking at a potential handball against Sam Nicholson – and he summoned Beaton to the monitor.

After review, the referee pointed to the spot.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

Kelechi Iheanacho stepped up and won it in the 99th minute with THE last kick of the ball.

It all sets up a final day showdown for the league title at Celtic Park on Saturday between Celtic and Hearts with the Jambos taking a one-point lead to Glasgow.

But the decision to award the penalty has proved highly contentious.



While the officials deemed it a handball, the TV punditry team felt that it had actually struck Nicholson on the HEAD.

And Hearts boss Derek McInnes agreed as he blasted the call as ‘disgusting.’

He told Sky Sports: “When you heard Celtic got a 96th minute penalty that was going to VAR and they were checking it, you just assume what’s happened is they get the penalty.



“Having seen it again, it’s disgusting. It is.

“I don’t think it’s a penalty kick.

“But we’re up against it. We’re up against everybody.

“We’ll be ready for Saturday.”

Asked if the decision would spark a ‘siege mentality’ heading to Parkhead, he added: “I don’t think it’s a penalty kick. There were two more shouts for a penalty kick at our game than Motherwell.



“If I’m Motherwell, I’m really disappointed with that having seen it again.

“I’ve seen it before I came out to speak to you and I think it’s so poor that they’ve been given that penalty.

“It looks as if they’ve been given it.

“They’ve been very fortunate on that side of it and we have to realise we are up against everything.

“We need to just go and deal with the game on Saturday.”



The decision was a sickener for Motherwell, too, as they were denied a point at the last moment.

It also means the battle for fourth will go to the final day with Well taking a one-point advantage over Hibs with the two teams meeting at Easter Road.

Motherwell boss Jens Berthel Askou was virtually speechless as he was asked to address the penalty decision.

He told Sky: “I think the big question is what are we even doing here?

“When things like that happen. I’m in total shock.



“I thought I had seen it all this year but apparently I haven’t.

“It’s shocking. It’s a shame for the game.

“I think we did everything we could and should to finish off really strong at Fir Park, finish where we started.



“A great game of football, I think coming back from 2-1, we did that really strongly, we didn’t hardly give anything away in the second half.

“Even after the game was supposed to be blown off, see that happening – it felt totally unreal looking at it on the TV footage.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“No matter how you read that situation, I can’t see anywhere where they can find a paragraph in the rule book where it can lead to a penalty.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola gives instructions to Crystal Palace stars ahead of defining Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola gives instructions to Crystal Palace stars ahead of defining Arsenal clash

Pep Guardiola's Manchester City side breezed past Crystal Palace before the Catalan was seeing chatting to a number of the Eagles' stars, who still need to play Arsenal this season

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was seen speaking to a number of Crystal Palace stars at full-time - less than two weeks before they play Arsenal (Image: Sky Sports)

Pep Guardiola went round several of the Crystal Palace players after Manchester City's win on Wednesday with suggestions he was rallying them to do his side a favour when they play Arsenal.

‌



At the Etihad, the title chasers secured a routine 3-0 win with Antoine Semenyo and Omar Marmoush among the goals. Savinho wrapped up the game in the second-half as City closed to within two points of league leaders Arsenal with two games remaining.

‌



The Gunners, eyeing their first title since 2004, will play Palace in the final game of the season at Selhurst Park. City will likely require a favour from the Eagles if they are to claim the title as they need Arsenal to slip up.

‌



Guardiola was all smiles all full-time as the Sky Sports pundits joked that he was going round the Palace players giving them advice. The Catalan was seen chatting with Jefferson Lerma, Maxence Lacroix and Adam Wharton.

Premier League title permutations as Arsenal and Man City race set to go down to wire READ MORE :

Man City breeze past Crystal Palace to keep pressure on Arsenal in title race READ MORE :

There is talk of Palace resting their top players for the final games of the season, although they put out a strong team for their trip to Manchester. Oliver Glasner's side have a Europa Conference League final to come later in May and the Austrian has suggested that he may manage his players' workload - but insists that won't impact the destination of the title.

Glasner recently claimed: “To be honest, if somebody criticises me, it would be nonsense. It’s just the last game but there are 37 games played before. That means if another team on matchday 25 rotated against City or Arsenal, they affected the title race as well."

‌



Guardiola's side will now shift their focus to their FA Cup final at the weekend as they take on Chelsea at Wembley. After that they will face Bournemouth before a final day of the season clash against Aston Villa. They will likely need six points if they want to become champions, but the City boss insists they can only put the pressure on.

View 2 Images Adam Wharton remains one of Crystal Palace's most influential players

"It depends on them [Arsenal]. If they win two games, nothing to do, nothing to talk," he said. "All we can be is in there just in case. The last two games are tough. And we all we can do now is go to sleep as quickly as possible and prepare for the FA Cup. That is what we have to do.

‌



"But it's not just FA Cup final, it's Bournemouth three days after. So travel to London, they [players] will be at home with wife and kids, so fatigue, fatigue."

Guardiola has never gone successive years without a league title in his managerial career, but after Liverpool won the league last term the possibility now exists that the City boss could be denied two years on the bounce after winning six in seven years.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker leads outrage at 'worst VAR decision yet' as Celtic get vital call in title fight
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker leads outrage at 'worst VAR decision yet' as Celtic get vital call in title fight

The race for the Scottish Premiership title is heating up between Celtic and Hearts

View 2 Images Celtic were awarded a last-minute penalty against Motherwell (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Lineker slammed what he perceived to be "the worst VAR decision" he'd ever seen during Celtic's clash with Motherwell on Wednesday evening. The Scottish Premiership titans are embroiled in a two-horse race for the league title with Hearts, just one point separating the two down the home stretch.

‌



After 37 games, Hearts lead the league standings with 80 points, while Celtic breathe down their neck on 79. And with just one match remaining, it's all still left to play for as Derek McInnes' and Martin O'Neill's sides meet in a title-decider at Celtic Park on Saturday.

‌



Celtic kept their title hopes alive thanks to a 3-2 win over Motherwell at Fir Park this week. Elliot Watt opened the scoring for the hosts just 17 minutes into play, before Daizen Maeda equalised just moments before half-time.

‌



Benjamin Nygren gave the Celts the lead 13 minutes into the second-half, as they looked to close out a 2-1 win over their domestic rivals and keep the pressure on Hearts - who took a 3-0 win over Falkirk simultaneously.

Fate had other plans for the encounter, however, when Liam Gordon equalised for Motherwell with just five minutes left on the clock, potentially crushing Celtic's dreams of an unprecedented 56th league title.

Things took an even bigger turn when Celtic were awarded a penalty 93 minutes into the clash. Sam Nicholson leapt for a looping throw in inside his own area with his arm raised - unclear as to whether the ball bounced off his hand of his forehead as he cleared it.

‌



Referee John Beaton was called upon by VAR Andrew Dallas to take a closer look at the situation, with the official ultimately awarding a spot-kick to Celtic - Kelechi Iheanacho stepping up to convert to ensure the title race proceeded to a last day decider come Saturday, May 16.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Sky Sports, HBO Max, Netflix and Disney+ with Ultimate TV package This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £44 Sky Get the deal here Product Description Sky has upgraded its Ultimate TV and Sky Sports bundle to now include HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu, as well as 135 channels and full Sky coverage of the Premier League and EFL. Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

‌



However, fans and pundits worldwide were unconvinced by the decision, with Lineker taking to X to write: "This might be the worst VAR decision I've seen (and there’s a lot of competition). Extraordinary given the significance."

Hearts manager McInnes, meanwhile, seethed at the call. He told Sky Sports in the aftermath: "When you heard Celtic had a 96th-minute penalty going to VAR, you just assume they get it.

"It's disgusting. We're up against it, we're up against everybody. I don't think it's a penalty. It's so poor and it looks as though [Celtic] have been given it. They have been very fortunate."

‌



Motherwell manager Jen Berthel Askou was also baffled by the decision. He said: "The big question is what are we even doing here. I'm in total shock. I thought I had seen it all this year, but apparently I haven't.

View 2 Images Gary Lineker was fuming (Image: PA)

"It's shocking and it's a shame for the game. Seeing the footage, I can't see any way that can be a penalty. I can't see it touch his hand and, even if it has, it's because his arm has been pushed into it. It's a crazy thing to be part of and the game deserved better than that."

Article continues below

On the other hand, O'Neill had very little argument that he believed it to be a foul, and subsequently, a penalty. He explained: "I have seen it back very, very briefly... it's a handball.

"It looks as if it's also an elbow to the side of the head as well. VAR have asked the referee to come over and he had no hesitation in giving the penalty."

As a result of the 3-2 win, the Scottish Premiership title all comes down to Celtic's encounter with Hearts on home soil this weekend, the winner taking all the marbles and glory for 2025/26.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel's year in review from first team plan to strong Rashford comments
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel's year in review from first team plan to strong Rashford comments

JJ Gabriel could be set to play a key role for Manchester United

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel is set to take centre stage in Thursday's FA Youth Cup final (Image: Getty)

Stars of the future will take to the pitch at the Joie Stadium on Thursday as Manchester United and Manchester City go head-to-head. The top two sides in the Under-18 Premier League square off in the FA Youth Cup final, with JJ Gabriel expected to play a pivotal role for United.

‌



The 15-year-old has dazzled in their youth teams this season, managing an impressive 26 goals in 28 appearances across the U18 Premier League and FA Youth Cup. That includes scoring United's opener in their 2-1 extra-time victory over Crystal Palace in the semi-finals.

‌



The sky is the limit for the most exciting talent currently within United's ranks. And all signs suggest one of the most in-demand youngsters in England is thriving as he edges closer to a potential first-team debut for United next season.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Big decision justified

Born in Enfield, Gabriel appeared far more likely to end up representing the likes of Arsenal or Tottenham than United. However, the club's scouting network deserves considerable credit for successfully luring him away from London.

And Gabriel's father, former Republic of Ireland international Joe O'Cearuill, has more reason than most to feel immense pride. He makes no attempt to hide it, either, having taken to social media previously to share his joy at the decision to relocate to the north in 2022.

‌



JJ Gabriel and Kai Rooney may face same decision after Man Utd first-team breakthrough READ MORE :

JJ Gabriel denied Man Utd reward given to Kobbie Mainoo as announcement made READ MORE :

"I remember in London when JJ was eight years old," he wrote in a since deleted post on X. "They used to say he [was] just a YouTuber and will never make it, just a showboat, he will be done at 11 years old. So glad we moved to Manchester. The club showed him love and let him grow into himself, not a robot."

It's bearing fruit so far, with Gabriel looking to further cement his rise by lifting the FA Youth Cup. He's already caught the eye of certain first-team figures at Old Trafford, too.

Rashford prediction

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has been talking Gabriel up on social media in recent months (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside, Offside via Getty Images)

‌



Though he may no longer be at the club, Marcus Rashford has already tipped his hat to Gabriel this season. Even from Barcelona, the former Old Trafford favourite has been keeping a close eye on a youngster carving out a path remarkably similar to his own.

Rashford, 28, celebrated winning La Liga with Barca on Sunday following a 2-0 win over Real Madrid in El Clasico. The England international played a pivotal role too, scoring a stunning free-kick at the Camp Nou.

A sea of stars from Rashford's past and present flooded Instagram to congratulate him on his triumph. Gabriel was among them, simply commenting "Top" on a celebratory post.

‌



Rashford appeared to acknowledge his successor in the comments section, replying: "Next up." That tribute clearly being a nod to the fact Gabriel is next in line to follow his same path from Carrington's academy and into the first team.

It's not the first time Rashford has placed the youngster on a pedestal, either, having previously championed United's next big thing. The senior star commented on one of Gabriel's Instagram posts in March and made his feelings about the forward clear, writing: "Lil bro is a star."

First team future

View 3 Images Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has taken note of Gabriel's clear talent (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



There is plenty of evidence to suggest United will welcome Gabriel into their first-team ranks next season. The club might have done so already were it not for Premier League regulations preventing him from featuring this campaign on account of his age.

The MEN reported in December how United were doing everything in their power to provide Gabriel with a clear route into the first team.This includes training sessions with the senior squad, and he has already been lined up to feature in this summer's pre-season tour of Europe.

Barcelona have registered an interest in the teenager and have already shown Gabriel around their facilities in an attempt to lure him away. However, those efforts have so far come to nothing.

‌



"Like everyone, I know he is a really talented guy and everyone paid attention on social media," said Ruben Amorim of the youngster when he was still at the helm in late 2025. "You could see the U21s had a game and we had less players and tried to pick players for training that have talent.

"Not just for me to see for tomorrow but for them to feel what it means to be in the first team, the difficulties playing against our defenders, the difficulty of our training, the pace. If we can use every training we have to show the kids what they need to do to be here, it is important, not just for JJ but for everyone."

Current interim manager Michael Carrick has equally taken note of the youngster's potential and said in March: "He's doing really well, JJ. We're always trying to give that exposure to players, for them to come and train and feel it.

Article continues below

"JJ is a big talent. It's pretty obvious to know that and he's had a really good season for the Under-18s. We obviously think an awful lot of him. But patience is important in managing everything that comes with that.

"It is about picking the right moment to step up, picking the moment to leave them in a certain place. What he's done when he's trained, he's done well as you'd expect."

Sports.title: Southampton boss could face BAN over Spygate saga as Saints delete Wembley ticket info
Sports.content:
Southampton boss could face BAN over Spygate saga as Saints delete Wembley ticket info

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert could yet face a ban for matches if the Saints are found guilty of SpyGate as the fallout continues ahead of an EFL hearing

View 2 Images Southampton boss Tonda Eckert could face a ban for his alleged involvement in the spying scandal if Southampton are found guilty (Image: Robin Jones, Getty Images)

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert or technical director Johannes Spors could face a ban if they are found to have ordered the alleged SpyGate mission that has engulfed the club.

‌



The Saints booked their place at Wembley this week by beating Middlesbrough in their play-off semi-final. Shea Charles' goal late in extra-time was good enough for victory, but it came after allegations of spying before the first-leg at the Riverside Stadium at the weekend.

‌



Southampton were charged by the EFL with misconduct after Boro allegedly caught a member of their analyst staff spying at their Rockliffe training ground. It has cast doubt over whether the south coast club will take on Hull for the right to play in the Premier League.

‌



The hearing, which is yet to be confirmed, will be conducted by an independent disciplinary commission. One of the possible outcomes, should Southampton be found guilty, could be to ban Eckert or Spors for matches, reports The Sun.

Southampton 'spy' named as he drops bank card clanger that could have huge ramifications READ MORE :

The alleged individual in question has been identified as intern William Salt. He was photographed hiding behind a tree using his mobile phone to spy on the Teessiders’ training session before he was confronted.

Salt has previously been photographed on the shoulder of Saints boss Eckert when he celebrated his Sky Bet Championship manager of the month award in February. He has not been included in more recent photos.

‌



Middlesbrough are ready to launch their case and are understood to have details of a credit card used by the individual at the golf club next to Rockliffe, part of the complex owned by Boro chairman Steve Gibson, which could potentially be part of a paper-trail that builds their case. Gibson has called upon the services of high-profile sports lawyer Nick De Marco and the Teesside club are calling for the EFL hearing to begin before the weekend so that clarity can be sought.

View 2 Images The SpyGate marred the play-off semi-final (Image: Robin Jones, Getty Images)

Kim Hellberg, who delivered an emotional response after Middlesbrough's season ended at St Mary's on Tuesday night, and his players are continuing to train as the possibility exists that Southampton could be expelled from the play-off final, which could see them reinstated.

Article continues below

In an embarrassing climb down Southampton have been forced to delete all ticketing updates, which they wrongly posted on Wednesday night as they shared information for the final. The club say the confusion over tickets was due to the fact they were meant to publish details at the same time as fellow finalists Hull.

Sports.title: World Cup final half-time show confirmed as Coldplay icon reveals three chosen artists
Sports.content:
World Cup final half-time show confirmed as Coldplay icon reveals three chosen artists

The World Cup final this summer will feature a half-time show for the first time with Madonna to perform alongside two other headline names at the MetLife Stadium

View Image The World Cup final will feature a half-time show (Image: Getty Images)

The first ever World Cup final half-time show will be co-headlined by Shakira, Madonna and BTS, FIFA announced early on Thursday morning.

‌



The blend of music from Latin, pop and Korea is seen as a collaboration that best reflects sounds from around the globe. The World Cup final will take place on July 19 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey

‌



The artists for the World Cup half-time show were selected by Coldplay lead Chris Martin, who shared the line-up in a video on social media that featured characters from Sesame Street and the Muppets. He told Elmo: “It’s a chance to show how amazing all different kinds of humans are."

‌



Madonna is the winner of seven Grammy Awards with her music career dating back decades whilst Colombian sensation Shakira has won four herself. BTS was the first K-pop group to receive a Grammy nomination.

Madonna headlined the Super Bowl halftime show in 2012, and Shakira shared the Super Bowl stage with Jennifer Lopez in 2020. That concept, which is common place in the NFL, will now filter into football as North American looks to combine sport and high profile entertainment.

Man Utd take huge step to appointing Michael Carrick with talks to open THIS WEEK READ MORE :

FIFA and Global Citizen conducted a trial half-time show at MetLife Stadium last summer during final of the FIFA Club World Cup, where Chelsea bat PSG. On that occasion it included the American rapper Doja Cat, the Nigerian singer Tems and the Colombian artist J Balvin. The performers sang from a stage that was built into the stands, but there is talk that the pitch could be used this summer, forcing a change to football's tradition schedule.

‌



Half-time during the final could therefore be notably longer than the standard 15 minutes. It would be the first time that the tournament will ignore the sport's usual quarter of an hour pause to put on entertainment

Content cannot be displayed without consent

In last year's Club World Cup final the half-time break lasted just over 24 minutes, rather than the 15 minutes that is set out in the Laws of the Game, as a result of the half-time entertainment.

‌



Now that the plans are announced several of those involved in the final will need to make amendments to their usual strategy. Coaches will have to consider how they conduct team talks with the break now longer than usual. Those involved in sports science will have to consider how the extended pause will impact on players.

Broadcasters will have a longer half-time period, which will alter their programming and schedules.

Sports.title: Man Utd's next moves after sorting midfield as £70m star arrives and left-back problem solved
Sports.content:
Man Utd's next moves after sorting midfield as £70m star arrives and left-back problem solved

Mancheter United could be shaping up for a big summer of incomings and outgoings

View 4 Images Carrick is rumoured to be involved in this summer's transfers (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

Manchester United are well aware that all of their hard-earned progress this season will count for nothing if they fail to bring in the right players come the summer transfer window. By securing Champions League football for next term, Michael Carrick has pulled off what was widely considered highly unlikely for much of the campaign under his predecessor, Ruben Amorim.

‌



While it remains unclear whether interim head coach Carrick will lead the side next season, he is understood to be advising the United hierarchy on potential summer signings.

‌



The prospect of Champions League football is likely to prove a considerable advantage for director of football Jason Wilcox in luring top talent, in stark contrast to last season, when the Reds missed out on Europe altogether and finished 15th in the league.

‌



Last summer, Wilcox clearly made the forward line his priority, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha for combined fees in excess of £200million.

There is little doubt that the midfield represents the most pressing concern this time around, having been a glaring weakness throughout the entire season. That issue looks set to intensify further, given Casemiro's imminent departure and the growing likelihood that Manuel Ugarte will also exit Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



That leaves Carrick, or whoever takes charge next term, without a holding midfielder. Further forward, options are equally thin on the ground, with Kobbie Mainoo and injury-prone Mason Mount being the only recognised No.8s at the club's disposal.

As such, a substantial spending spree is anticipated on two, or potentially even three, midfield additions. According to recent reports, combative Atalanta midfielder Ederson is amongst the most probable new arrivals this summer.

View 4 Images Ederson could be on his way to Man United this summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



According to Fabrizio Romano, United are in discussions with the 26-year-old Brazilian's agent regarding personal terms. He has featured on United's shortlist of potential recruits since last year.

They can secure Ederson for a highly reasonable fee of around £40m, bringing some much-needed reinforcement to the engine room. Yet, if Ederson represents the floor-raiser, United also require a midfielder capable of raising the ceiling.

Reports indicate Old Trafford chiefs are keen to land one marquee signing who could command a fee of up to £80m. Elliot Anderson remains their top target, though they may need to look elsewhere should Forest demand a Premier League record-breaking transfer for the midfielder, surpassing Florian Wirtz's £116m move to Liverpool.

‌



Given Manchester City's interest, United would be shrewd to sidestep a bidding war and therefore any deal that would cost upwards of £100m to secure the England international. In that scenario, Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton, who United have also been monitoring, represents a financially astute alternative.

View 4 Images Manchester United have been linked with a transfer for both Adam Wharton and Elliot Anderson (Image: (Photo by Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images))

The 22-year-old, who is also expected to feature for the Three Lions at this summer's World Cup, could command a fee of £70-80m but would nonetheless bring some much-needed quality to the squad. Wharton is perhaps the closest current Premier League player to Carrick in his prime, with the ability to dictate play from deep.

‌



United are also known to have their eye on Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who is valued at around £50m. The 22-year-old is a serious midfield contender in Wilcox's thinking, despite being a less high-profile name than the likes of Carlos Baleba and Sandro Tonali.

Having secured Ederson and Wharton, Scott's arrival would depend on how much revenue United can generate through player sales, with other areas of the squad also requiring urgent reinforcement. Central defence is one such area, given Harry Maguire's age, and the injury-prone records of Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt.

Cristian Romero and Micky van de Ven are two top-class defenders who could push for an exit following Tottenham's dreadful campaign. However, Forest's Murillo is the player United ought to be targeting instead.

‌



View 4 Images Murillo has been linked with a move to United in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

The tenacious Brazilian is one of Forest's most vital assets and could carry a substantial price tag of £60-70m. At this stage, with United's squad stretched across Europe, the League Cup and the FA Cup next season, it is a sum they simply cannot afford to shy away from. Completing what promises to be a hectic summer will be the pursuit of a left-back.

The heavy dependence on Luke Shaw is simply not sustainable going forward, while Patrick Dorgu has proved his worth further up the pitch under Carrick. Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert is amongst the names that have been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

Article continues below

Truffert has reportedly attracted the attention of the scouting team, having made a strong impression on the south coast since joining last summer. The Frenchman has featured for the full duration of all but two Premier League matches for the Cherries this season, underlining his consistency.

Sports.title: Chelsea already received Xabi Alonso green light as manager decides on new job
Sports.content:
Chelsea already received Xabi Alonso green light as manager decides on new job

Chelsea are pursuing Xabi Alonso in the hope the Spaniard will become the club's new long-term head coach

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is reportedly in talks to become the next Chelsea manager (Image: SOPA Images, SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso had already expressed his interest in managing in the Premier League before reports emerged claiming he is open to the Chelsea job. Alonso features on the Blues' shortlist for a new permanent manager, following the sacking of Liam Rosenior in April.

‌



Chelsea have opened talks with the Spaniard's representatives and, according to The Athletic, the 44-year-old is interested in taking charge at Stamford Bridge this summer.

‌



It may surprise some given Alonso's connections with Liverpool, where he lifted the Champions League as a player and had been tipped to replace Arne Slot due to his disastrous campaign in charge of the Reds. But Slot is expected to keep his job despite mounting pressure and even boos from his own fans during Saturday's 1-1 draw with Chelsea.

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alonso's blocked return to Liverpool makes his desire to become Chelsea's new manager less of a surprise. That is especially true considering he admitted two years ago that he was intrigued by the possibility of managing in the Premier League one day, while still at Bayer Leverkusen.

When the subject of working in the Premier League arose during a pre-match press conference in April 2024, Alonso said: You never know. At the moment I have enough on my plate to think about but I'm still young as a coach and for sure it's a nice thought."

‌



Chelsea add three new names to next manager shortlist as Cesc Fabregas stance confirmed READ MORE :

Real Madrid icon Iker Casillas sums up Bernabeu chaos with next manager pick READ MORE :

Alonso had just turned down Liverpool by committing to Bayer Leverkusen as the Reds tried to bring in the Spaniard to replace Jurgen Klopp. The decision followed Alonso's remarkable season with the German side.

The former World Cup winner's reputation reached an all-time high after steering Leverkusen from near-relegation to an unbeaten domestic double and the Europa League final in 2023/24. He remained in Germany for another campaign, which proved more challenging, before taking the helm at Real Madrid last summer - another of his former clubs.

View 2 Images Many thought Alonso would end up at Liverpool after admitting he was open to becoming a manager in the Premier League (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Alonso left his role in the Spanish capital after less than eight months in charge. Lacklustre results, question marks over his tactics and reports of unrest in the dressing room were rumoured to be the causes of his exit, which was described as a "mutual agreement".

Looking ahead to his potential arrival at Chelsea, the Blues are aiming to have a new head coach in place by mid-June. Whether or not they secure Champions League qualification, the club are preparing for a busy summer and plan to bring in at least a new centre-back, central midfielder and left-sided winger.

Alonso, based on suggestions he is open to the Chelsea job, does not appear to be put off by the failure of the Blues' managers under the club's new ownership in recent times. Rosenior survived just 106 days at Stamford Bridge as Enzo Maresca's successor, paying the price for a dreadful run of results that looks likely to deny Chelsea a Champions League spot.

Sports.title: Man United's 2022 FA Youth Cup winners now including 'New Ronaldo' sold for £40million
Sports.content:
Man United's 2022 FA Youth Cup winners now including 'New Ronaldo' sold for £40million

There's been a series of highs and lows for members of the Manchester United squad that won the FA Youth Cup in 2022

View 6 Images United won the FA Youth Cup in 2022 (Image: 2022 Getty Images)

Manchester United will face Manchester City in the FA Youth Cup final on Thursday, with United aiming to lift the trophy for the first time since 2022. United are the most decorated club in Youth Cup history, having won the competition 11 times.

‌



However, they've only secured it twice since the turn of the Millennium, highlighting what a significant accomplishment the 2022 success represented. The 3-1 win over Nottingham Forest four years ago displayed a wealth of talent within United's ranks.

‌



From players who have generated substantial transfer fees for United to those who have progressed to the first team, Mirror Football examines where the squad from the 2022 winning side are now.

‌



Radek Vitek - Goalkeeper

Vitek was the goalkeeper who featured in the 2022 FA Youth Cup Final. The 23-year-old Czech Republic stopper remains on United's books but is yet to make a first-team appearance. He has been loaned out to Bristol City this season, featuring in 41 matches for the Championship outfit.

View 6 Images Radek Vitek is still on the books at United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Marc Jurado - Right back

Jurado, 22, featured at right-back in the 2022 final. However, United offloaded the former Barcelona prospect on transfer deadline day of 2023 to Espanyol. He subsequently joined FC Cartagena, who compete in the Spanish third tier.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford finally confirms his true desire around Man Utd and Barcelona transfer READ MORE :

Man Utd told Casemiro's ideal replacement amid Aurelien Tchouameni and Joao Gomes transfer link READ MORE :

Louis Jackson - Centre-back

Jackson was a standout performer against Forest. The 20-year-old remains based at Carrington, where he continues to turn heads. He spent this season on loan at National League outfit Solihull Moors.

Rhys Bennett - Centre-back

Bennett netted United's opening goal in the FA Youth Cup Final and lifted the trophy. The 22-year-old earned a spot on the first-team bench under former United manager Erik ten Hag but never made it onto the pitch. He has had loan spells at Stockport County and put pen to paper with Fleetwood Town this year.

‌



View 6 Images Rhys Bennett holds the FA Youth Cup in 2022 (Image: 2022 Getty Images)

Sam Murray - Left-back

Left-back Murray, 21, penned a new deal with United in 2023 but was let go by the club in 2025. Murray has since joined National League side Carlisle United.

Kobbie Mainoo - Centre-midfield

One of the standout talents from the 2022 winning squad, Mainoo grabbed the winner in the FA Youth Cup Final and has firmly established himself in United's first team. He started England's showdown with Spain in the Euro 2024 final and recently committed to a new five-year contract at United after catching the eye under interim boss Michael Carrick.

‌



View 6 Images Kobbie Mainoo recently signed a new deal at United (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Dan Gore - Centre-midfield

The 21-year-old midfielder made his United senior bow in the Carabao Cup win against Crystal Palace in 2023 but has yet to feature for the first team since. Gore is currently on his third loan spell at Rotherham United, where he has racked up 34 appearances this season.

Isak Hansen-Aaroen - Attacking-midfield

The 21-year-old attacking midfielder was held in high esteem at United. However, having failed to break into the first team, the Norwegian moved to Werder Bremen in early 2024. He was subsequently sent out on loan to Danish club Aalborg before completing a permanent switch to Dutch side NEC Nijmegen this year.

‌



View 6 Images Isak Hansen-Aaroen was highly regarded at United (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images.)

Sam Mather - Right-wing

The versatile 21-year-old winger featured at right wing in the FA Youth Cup final and had brief loan stints at Rochdale and Tranmere Rovers thereafter. He departed United for Turkish outfit Kayserispor in January 2026, where he has made two appearances this season.

Alejandro Garnacho - Left-wing

Garnacho was another standout success from the Youth Cup-winning squad. He netted twice in the match, which served as a springboard for his career at Old Trafford. Garnacho, who at one staged was dubbed the heir to Cristiano Ronaldo at Old Trafford went on to score 26 first-team goals in 144 appearances for United, including a strike in the 2024 FA Cup Final, before leaving for Chelsea last summer for £40million.

‌



View 6 Images Alejandro Garnacho has endured a challenging start to his Chelsea career (Image: (Photo by James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Charlie McNeill - Striker

McNeill, 22, was a prolific marksman throughout United's youth ranks. He netted 600 goals at youth level for Manchester City prior to his move to United. He played a pivotal role in the club's run to the Youth Cup Final but penned a deal with Sheffield Wednesday in 2024, where he has established himself as a regular, finding the net six times in 50 appearances.

Substitutes

Sonny Aljofree – The 21-year-old entered the fray as an 86th-minute substitute and remains at United, having spent this season on loan at Notts County.

‌



Maxi Oyedele – Oyedele is now a fully established Polish international who turns out for Strasbourg following his departure from United in 2024. He came on as a 64th-minute substitute in the 2022 final.

Joe Hugill – After a string of loan spells, Hugill, 22, signed for Kilmarnock this year.

Logan Pye – Logan Pye, 22, spent three years progressing through United's youth ranks before completing a permanent switch to Burnley in September 2023.

‌



Tom Wooster – The 21-year-old goalkeeper was let go by United in the summer of 2025 to link up with West Ham United.

Omari Forson – Forson made four appearances for the United first team, but the 21-year-old winger departed the club for Italian outfit Monza in 2024 on a free transfer.

Ethan Ennis – Ennis, 21, began his career at United's rivals Liverpool before making the move to United in 2017 and remains on the club's books. The highly-regarded winger has spent time on loan at Doncaster Rovers and Fleetwood Town across the past two seasons.

Sports.title: Harden scores 30 points as Cavaliers beat Pistons in overtime
Sports.content:
James Harden scored a playoff-best 30 points and Donovan Mitchell had 21, helping the Cleveland Cavaliers come back from a nine-point deficit late in regulation and beat the Detroit Pistons 117-113 in overtime on Wednesday night to take a 3-2 lead in their Eastern Conference semi-finals series.

The Pistons led by 15 points in the first half and 103-94 with two-plus minutes left. The Cavs rallied and pulled into a 103-all tie on Evan Mobley's free throws with 45.2 seconds left.

Cleveland went on a 13-0 run and held Detroit scoreless for five minutes from late in fourth quarter to midway through overtime. The Cavs went ahead by seven with 2:39 left in overtime on Mitchell's 3-pointer.

Cade Cunningham, who had 39 points and nine assists, made a jumper to pull the Pistons within two points with 25 seconds left.

Harden made one free throw on the ensuing possession and rebounded his missed second attempt. He made another free throw to help seal the win.

Sports.title: 2am finish! Coppa Italia final fireworks cause chaos at Italian Open
Sports.content:
Italy’s Luciano Darderi had to deal with a smoke delay resulting from fireworks at the Coppa Italia final at the neighbouring Stadio Olimpico before eventually beating teenager Rafael Jodar to reach the Italian Open semi-finals, in a match that finished just after 2am local time.

The quarter-final was delayed for nearly 20 minutes towards the end of the first set as smoke wafted in from fireworks that had been set off at the Stadio Olimpico after Inter Milan beat Lazio 2-0 in Italian football's domestic cup final.

Darderi was complaining that he could not see anything and the smoke was also affecting the cameras for the electronic line-calling system, which had to be reset.

When play resumed, Darderi held serve to take the set to a tiebreaker, where he found himself 5-2 down before rallying.

The 24-year-old Darderi, who on at least a couple of occasions was drinking coffee during changeovers, broke immediately in the second set. Jodar managed to break back and then fend off two match points before levelling the match.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Italian Open quarter-final match between Rafael Jodar and Luciano Darderi

Darderi dominated the decider and sealed the result 7-6 (7-5), 5-7, 6-0 when Jodar hit a forehand into the net, securing his first place in a Masters 1000 semi-final.

He will now play Casper Ruud, who earlier overcame 13th-ranked Karen Khachanov 6-1 1-6 6-2 after a match suspended by more than two hours at the start of the second set by rain.
